title: Adaptive admission regulator for phased model launches
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement an admission regulator service and declarative policy DSL to orchestrate phased model launches across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The regulator enforces step schedules, traffic splits, cohort guards, shadow verification probes, and auto-rollback hysteresis based on metric contracts (latency, error-rate, cost delta, and quality regressions). This work covers schema, control-plane APIs, a lightweight runtime validator, telemetry hooks for Console, and e2e tests for behaviour under noisy telemetry and infra flakiness.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL that expresses: ordered steps, per-step traffic fractions, delay windows, stop conditions and explicit rollback rules
Runtime evaluator that can evaluate policies against live telemetry and emit deterministic decisions (advance, hold, rollback)
Support for shadow traffic probes with configurable sampling and comparators to surface mismatches to Console
Auto-rollback with hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping: configurable grace periods and escalation paths
Per-cohort routing rules (cookie/identity-based) and population-aware splits for A/B tests
End-to-end tests that simulate latency spikes, regression signals, and partial infra loss demonstrating safe holds/rollbacks
Console integration: rollout timeline, per-step metric carpets, and a single-click abort/accelerate control

2026-03-10 - Jamal Singh: Changed default auto-rollback hysteresis to require two consecutive breach windows to avoid oscillation. Updated DSL examples in design doc and unit tests. Next: proto deployment to staging Dedicated cluster and shadow testing against live traffic for two days.
